also: how much difference does it make?

terms.grammar: verb: impersonal, from intersum; inter … et … for the things compared
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.11: inter hominem et bēluam hoc maximē interest
Ter. Ad. 76: hoc pater ac dominus interest
terms.comment: Latin usually says “difference” with the verb: quid interest inter … et …?, what’s the difference between … and …?; multum interest, it makes a big difference; nihil interest, there’s no difference (see it makes no difference).

evidence: Cic. Balb. 49: sit hoc discrīmen inter grātiōsōs cīvēs atque fortēs (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Off. 1.94: honestī et decōrī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A word of philosophy and of teaching (Cicero, Quintilian).

phrases.latin: Dī inmortālēs, hominī homō quid praestat? stultō intellegēns quid inter est?
phrases.english: Good gods, how one man can outdo another! What a difference there is between a fool and a man of sense!

phrases.latin: Hoc pater ac dominus interest: hoc quī nequit, fateātur nescīre imperāre līberīs.
phrases.english: That is the difference between a father and a master; whoever can’t do it should admit he doesn’t know how to bring up children.

phrases.latin: sed inter hominem et bēluam hoc maximē interest, quod haec tantum, quantum sēnsū movētur, ad id sōlum, quod adest quodque praesēns est, sē accommodat
phrases.english: but the chief difference between man and beast is this: the beast, as far as its senses move it, adapts itself only to what is here and now
How much difference does it make?
